preamble: Denasalization of the glottalized alveolar nasal [nˀ] (Americanist n̓) to plain [d]. In Makah the Proto-Southern-Wakashan (PSW) nasals became voiced stops and the glottalized sonorants merged with the plain ones, lengthening the preceding vowel (Davidson 2002: 76, citing Jacobsen 1968). PSW *n̓ therefore appears as Makah d, while Nuu-chah-nulth keeps n̓: Nuu-chah-nulth čun̓a, Makah ču·da 'vulva'. The same correspondence recurs in suffixes listed by Davidson. For Quileute, Wikipedia's summary of Powell (1974) gives Proto-Chimakuan *n̓ > Quileute d or ʔd (Chemakum n or ʔn), without a word example. The word evidence here comes from Makah alone.

languageExamples.context: Davidson (2002: 76): the Proto-Southern-Wakashan glottalized sonorants merged with the plain sonorants in Makah, with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel (citing Jacobsen 1968); Nuu-chah-nulth keeps them; the nasal also became a stop, as plain *n did

examples.note: Davidson (2002: 76), ex. (127). The long u· before d is the compensatory lengthening.
